register.text: EU grants and loans under NextGenerationEU for reforms and investments agreed with Romania, paid in instalments against milestones and targets. register.text: The tram tranche of a €300 million EIB loan to the Municipality of Bucharest, for the renovation of around 50 kilometres of tram tracks with their platforms and contact network, new trams and depot upgrades. dispatches.label: 17 Nov 2026
dispatches.author: steward
dispatches.title: EIB releases €400 million to extend Romania’s Cernavodă nuclear unit
dispatches.summary: The European Investment Bank has released the first €400 million of a planned €800 million to Nuclearelectrica, for up to 22 years, to refurbish Unit 1 of the Cernavodă nuclear plant and extend its life by 30 years.
body: On 17 November 2026 the European Investment Bank announced a first loan tranche of €400 million to Nuclearelectrica, the operator of the Cernavodă nuclear power plant. It is half of the €800 million that the bank’s Board of Directors approved in July 2026, and the loan runs for up to 22 years.

Nuclearelectrica is 82.49 percent held by the Romanian state. The refurbishment costs €3.1 billion in total; the rest of the financing is being negotiated with export credit agencies, commercial banks, international financial institutions and Nuclearelectrica itself. The release does not state the interest rate or when the second tranche will be signed.

The money finances component replacements and system upgrades at Unit 1, which would extend its operational life by 30 years, subject to regulatory compliance. Work on the reactor starts in 2027 and lasts three years. The plant’s two units together generate around 20 percent of Romania’s electricity.
It moves energy, one of the seven standards: it keeps a low-carbon source of about a fifth of the nation’s electricity running for three more decades, rather than replacing it.

The structure could work for another nation. A long development-bank loan to a state-majority operator, released in tranches and paired with export credit agencies, could finance the life extension of an existing plant in Bulgaria in the same way.
